records.issue_text: [BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so a slot whose start falls inside working hours but which extends past the working-hours end is never rejected. A 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before workingHours.endTime passes the check (`end` equals `start`, which is < endTime), so getSchedule returns slots that overrun the host's working hours; users book events the host never agreed to host. Note also the whole workingHours branch is only reachable for slots on days without overrides, so every normal (non-override) day's slot validation now depends on this broken comparison.

records.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the newly added date-override logic can short-circuit before the busy-time checks. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The working-hours rejection predicate is inverted relative to its intent: it returns `true` from `find` (leading to `return false`) when `start < workingHour.startTime` — i.e. it rejects slots that start before opening, which is correct — but because `end` equals `start` (see separate finding) the intended 'slot overruns closing time' rule is unreachable, leaving a half-implemented rule shipped. Callers relying on this filter for boundary enforcement get asymmetric protection: early starts blocked, late overruns allowed. records.issue_text: [BUG] When a slot falls on a date that has an override but the find callback returns undefined (slot inside the override window, or the override doesn't fully rule it out), `dateOverrideExist` short-circuits to `return true` without consulting `busy` — the availability check for busy times is entirely skipped for any slot on an overridden date. A slot on an overridden date that collides with an existing booking passes checkIfIsAvailable because the busy check is bypassed; double-bookings become bookable on any day with a date override.
records.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the newly added date-override logic can short-circuit before the busy-time checks. After scanning `dateOverrides`, if any override exists for the slot’s day, it sets `dateOverrideExist = true`, and if the slot is not outside the override window it reaches `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`. This returns immediately and bypasses the later `return busy.every((busyTime) => { ... })` block, so calendar/booking busy events are not considered for slots on override days within the override window, potentially offering already-busy times as available.
